tex_content.html: \begin{example} \end{example}[Axial Isometries] 1. ch12:12.20Every nontrivial Euclidean translation is axial, with axes parallel to its translation vector. In the upper half-plane model, a dilation $(x,y)\mapsto (cx,cy)$ with $c\ne 1$ is axial with axis $\gamma (t)=(0,e^t)$; nontrivial horizontal translations are not axial. \end{example}
